evidence.reference_title: Increased capsaicin receptor TRPV1-expressing sensory fibres in irritable bowel syndrome and their correlation with abdominal pain.
evidence.snippet: Increased TRPV1 nerve fibres are observed in IBS, together with a low-grade inflammatory response. The increased TRPV1 nerve fibres may contribute to visceral hypersensitivity and pain in IBS, and provide a novel therapeutic target.

evidence.reference_title: Mast cell-dependent excitation of visceral-nociceptive sensory neurons in irritable bowel syndrome.
evidence.snippet: IBS-dependent excitation of dorsal root ganglia was inhibited by histamine H(1) receptor blockade and serine protease inactivation (inhibition of 51.7%; P < .05 and 74.5%; P < .05; respectively).

nodes.description: Excess bile acids reach the colon in a subset of patients meeting criteria for diarrhoea-predominant IBS. In primary bile acid diarrhoea the proposed cause is overproduction rather than an ileal defect: reduced ileal FGF19 release weakens feedback inhibition of hepatic bile acid synthesis, so the bile acid pool exceeds the ileum's capacity to reabsorb it. Measurable with SeHCAT retention, serum C4 or FGF19, and treatable with bile acid sequestrants.

evidence.reference_title: Systematic review with meta-analysis: the prevalence of bile acid malabsorption in the irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea.
evidence.snippet: These data provide evidence that in excess of one quarter of patients meeting accepted criteria for IBS-D have bile acid malabsorption.

evidence.reference_title: A new mechanism for bile acid diarrhea: defective feedback inhibition of bile acid biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: We propose a mechanism whereby impaired FGF19 feedback inhibition causes excessive bile acid synthesis that exceeds the normal capacity for ileal reabsorption, producing bile acid diarrhea.
Some mechanisms can be quantified using validated tests and questionnaires, including abnormal bile acid metabolism, accelerated colonic transit, and psychological comorbidity.

nodes.description: Bile acid binders for patients with diarrhoea in whom bile acid malabsorption has been shown by SeHCAT or a serum or faecal bile acid test.

evidence.reference_title: Meta-Analysis: Efficacy and Safety of Sequestrants for Bile Acid Diarrhoea.
evidence.snippet: Bile acid diarrhoea, a common cause of diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome, has a similar prevalence to coeliac disease and inflammatory bowel diseases. The mainstay of treatment is bile acid sequestrants (BAS).

evidence.reference_title: Meta-Analysis: Efficacy and Safety of Sequestrants for Bile Acid Diarrhoea.
evidence.snippet: Meta-analysis of parallel-design trials of sequestrants only showed a clinically significant reduction in stool consistency and frequency with pooled relative risks of 1.50 (95% CI: 1.14-1.96) and 2.80 (95% CI: 1.68-4.67), respectively.

evidence.reference_title: A diet low in FODMAPs reduces symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Bloating, pain, and passage of wind also were reduced while IBS patients were on the low-FODMAP diet.

evidence.reference_title: Intestinal membrane permeability and hypersensitivity in the irritable bowel syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Approximately 39% of diarrhea-predominant IBS patients had increased intestinal membrane permeability as measured by the lactulose/mannitol ratio.

evidence.reference_title: Role of serotonin in the pathophysiology of the irritable bowel syndrome.
evidence.snippet: 5-HT directly and indirectly affects intestinal motor and secretory function and abnormalities may lead to either constipation or diarrhea.

evidence.reference_title: Low-FODMAP Diet Improves Irritable Bowel Syndrome Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis
evidence.snippet: the patients receiving a low-FODMAP diet experienced a statistically significant pain and bloating reduction compared with those receiving a traditional diet

nodes.description: Supplementation of an established low-FODMAP diet with a blend of high-amylose maize resistant starch (HAMS) and psyllium husk, as an adjunct aimed at the microbial cost of FODMAP restriction rather than at symptom control. Distinct from psyllium monotherapy: the single trial reporting it used a psyllium-matched placebo, so the effects below are the incremental effect of the resistant-starch component on a psyllium background, not an effect of psyllium. Investigational — one small unreplicated preprint trial, with no guideline standing.

evidence.reference_title: Dietary fibre blend improves gut health in patients with Irritable Bowel Syndrome following a low FODMAP diet: a randomised, double-blind control trial
evidence.snippet: ur gut® improved GI-specific anxiety (P = 0.01) and sexual subscale of QOL (P = 0.018).

evidence.reference_title: Dietary fibre blend improves gut health in patients with Irritable Bowel Syndrome following a low FODMAP diet: a randomised, double-blind control trial
evidence.snippet: observed intervention effects were not due to psyllium husk, the placebo incorporated

nodes.description: Altered composition and function of gut microbiota may contribute to symptoms. Post-infectious IBS follows gastroenteritis in some patients. Genus-level composition is modifiable by dietary fermentable substrate: adding high-amylose resistant starch to a low-FODMAP diet shifts composition and enriches the resistant-starch degrader Ruminococcus E. Whether such a shift moves the community toward a healthy-donor reference is untested, as the trials reporting it carry no healthy-control arm.

evidence.reference_title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome and the Gut Microbiome: A Comprehensive Review.
evidence.snippet: Although the pathophysiology of IBS has not been fully elucidated, it involves dysregulation of communication between the brain and gut (brain-gut axis) which is associated with alterations in intestinal motility, gut permeability, visceral hypersensitivity and gut microbiota composition.

evidence.reference_title: Dietary fibre blend improves gut health in patients with Irritable Bowel Syndrome following a low FODMAP diet: a randomised, double-blind control trial
evidence.snippet: A specific mix of fibres can increase fibre intake, improve gut microbiota and gastrointestinal-specific anxiety without impacting sleep and symptoms of IBS patients on a low FODMAP diet as compared with placebo, despite no changes found in faecal and blood biomarkers.
